The search was inhibited by the arduous terrain and the threat of further avalanches. A large rescue team was waiting at the alpine camp to be flown in by helicopter at dawn on Tuesday, Sept. 8, to continue the search, weather permitting, according to the report. sentences: "> Mainland Spain endured its hottest summer since records began in 1961, with an unprecedented 61 heatwave days across June, July and August, national weather agency AEMET said on Wednesday.
In Spain, the Carlos III Health Institute has estimated more than 5,000 heat-related deaths from June to August, a record since its statistics began in 2015.

AEMET said the 10 hottest summers on record in Spain have all come in the 21st century.
Exceptional heat has also spilled over the traditional limits of summer, with high temperatures measured in late May and early September.

In late July, a blaze just dozens of kilometres west of Madrid sparked the evacuation of tens of thousands of people, with authorities describing it at the time as the largest wildfire in Spain's recent history.

A string of exceptional summer heatwaves have smashed temperature records across Europe this year, which scientists say human-driven climate change has intensified and lengthened.
This year's number of summer heatwave days obliterated the previous high of 41 from 2022.
On September 2, the southwestern municipality of El Granado reached 45.7C, equalling the temperature record for the month and marking the highest temperature in Spain this year.
According to the European Forest Fire Information System, almost 296,000 hectares (731,000 acres) have gone up in smoke in Spain this year as of September 2.
